extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature: practicing scientists and educated general readers (marine biologists, zoologists, chemists, economists, historians of science)
extracted.subtask_description: A mixed journal-issue excerpt containing methodological commentary (marine sampling, adhesives testing), a book review, and short scientific notes — i.e., assessment of scientific methods and scholarly works for a broad scientific readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on common species that make up the bulk
rubrics_metrics.description: “the main thing is to know the animals that make up the great bulk of the bottom population, to know their distribution and their weight per square mile.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritise identification and quantification of the common, characteristic species (those that determine community structure and biomass) rather than rare species when the goal is understanding overall bottom-fauna patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling intensity proportional to desired exactitude
rubrics_metrics.description: “If you wish for greater exactitude than this first trip could give, you may take more stations and investigate smaller areas more carefully.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the number of sampling stations and the spatial resolution according to the precision required; increase station density and reduce area per station for more exact quantitative estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bottom-sampler yields true, quantitative representative illustration
rubrics_metrics.description: The bottom-sampler “is able to give a true and quantitative representative illustration of the bottom fauna,” allowing statements about communities and quantitative ideas of animal abundance and seasonal variation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use bottom-sampling devices when the objective is quantitative community description (species composition per unit area, community types, temporal changes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dredge provides a biased, non-quantitative assemblage
rubrics_metrics.description: A dredge “is inclined… to take all animals on, not in, the bottom… therefore not a true illustration of what is living in or on the bottom, but a mixture mostly of epi-fauna… without giving the slightest idea of quantity per square metre.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat dredge catches as presence/collecting tools (good for rare/epifaunal specimens) but not as quantitative measures of infaunal community density or representative community composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare and interpret differences between gear types
rubrics_metrics.description: “The content of a dredge and a bottom-sampler used on the same station will very often give quite different collections of animals.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect and interpret systematic differences between sampling gears; use complementary methods (sampler + dredge) when both quantitative structure and rare/epifaunal taxa are of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know limitations and modify apparatus for context
rubrics_metrics.description: “The bottom-sampler is not able to solve every question; it cannot, e.g., take animals living very deep in a hard bottom, and the apparatus must be modified for special work, according to the size of the ship used, the depth at which you are working, etc., and it is necessary to supplement the investigation by means of other apparatus, fishing-gear, dredges, etc.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapt sampling equipment to substrate, depth, and vessel constraints; plan supplementary techniques for habitats or organisms the primary gear cannot sample.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative work required to understand principal features
rubrics_metrics.description: “But without quantitative work it is not possible to understand the principal features of the fauna of the sea-bottom.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For ecological understanding (productivity, fisheries implications, spatial/temporal patterns) implement quantitative sampling and measurement rather than qualitative or anecdotal records alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanical tensile test as primary glue-value criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: “The only criterion of its value as adhesive is a mechanical test of a glued joint between wooden test pieces of specified nature and size. The report describes the conditions of such a test, as finally adopted, and sets forth the possible sources of error.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use standardised mechanical joint-break tests (specified substrates, dimensions, conditioning) as the main operational measure of adhesive performance; document test conditions and potential error sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search for simple measurable correlates of glue strength
rubrics_metrics.description: “it is desirable to find some easily measured constant which shows a simple quantitative relation with the breaking strength… No such constant is yet known, although empirically the setting time of the glue sol, the melting point of the gel and its ‘strength,’ i.e. roughly speaking, its modulus of elasticity, furnish some indication of its quality.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate proxies (setting time, gel melting point, elastic modulus) as practical predictors of tensile strength, but validate correlations before substituting them for mechanical tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for non-gelatin constituents in adhesive performance
rubrics_metrics.description: “It is known that pure gelatin is not a good adhesive, so that the superiority of glue must be due, directly or indirectly, to the presence of other substances of which, so far, little is known.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyse and characterise minor or extractable constituents; do not assume base polymer composition alone explains adhesive behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diffusible-nitrogen test as a diagnostic for adhesives
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee’s novel test for “diffusible nitrogen”: “A gel of standard composition is immersed in a known volume of water, and after a fixed time the nitrogen content of the latter is determined by Kjeldahl’s method… amount of diffusible nitrogen is roughly inversely proportional to the tensile strength.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat diffusible-nitrogen as a promising but not definitive indicator (exceptions noted); use it alongside mechanical tests and chemical characterisation rather than as a sole measure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chemical/analytical confirmation required before strong claims
rubrics_metrics.description: In the tungsten-decomposition note the authors “emphasise the necessity of complete analysis of the gas obtained before anything conclusive can be stated.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid premature conclusions based on preliminary spectral/qualitative observations; perform complete chemical analyses to confirm identities before publicity or strong claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical evidence needed for social-science claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Critique of Edgeworth: “practically no scientific investigation has yet been made of the relative efficiency of men and women in different occupations.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rest policy or generalisations on untested assumptions about relative abilities; design and cite empirical studies before asserting productivity or efficiency differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scrutinise normative economic assumptions in policy proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: On endowment of motherhood the reviewer warns that assuming redistribution from rich to poor (and that this is objectionable) is “questionable ground.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating policy proposals, make explicit and critically examine assumptions about redistribution and social effects rather than treating them as settled.

rubrics_metrics.name: A new scholarly book must offer new matter or ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: “a new volume is liable to be subjected to scrutiny to see whether it can justify its birth by furnishing new matter or new ideas.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess new works for originality and whether they fill genuine gaps in the literature before recommending them as necessary additions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use ethnological/comparative evidence for archaeological interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer notes the book “would have gained by a wider reference to evidence derived from ethnological sources… Ethnological data must be brought to bear upon archaeological research if an adequate diagnosis of early customs and appliances is to be achieved.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In historical/archaeological syntheses, incorporate ethnographic and comparative data to strengthen interpretation of scarce or ambiguous material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain zoological accuracy and precise terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer points out several “termino‑zoological inexactitudes” (e.g., classing dolphins as fishes, misidentifying fishes on plates, including shell-fish among fishes prohibited by Moses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure taxonomic and terminological correctness in scientific writing and illustrations; such errors undermine scientific credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance speculation with evidence; avoid special pleading
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewer says the author “revels in argument, and while now and then he may, perhaps, be suspected of ‘special pleading,’ his interpretations… are always interesting and suggestive, even when he fails to be entirely convincing.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag and qualify speculative interpretations; distinguish hypothesis from demonstrated fact and avoid rhetorical bias or forced interpretations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide good illustrations and comprehensive bibliography
rubrics_metrics.description: Praise that “The illustrations are both good and numerous” and that the report is “supplemented by an appendix… giving a ‘Descriptive Bibliography of ‘Gelatin.’ This is a very complete, lucid, and impartial summary of the vast literature.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enhance scholarly works with clear, numerous illustrations and a thorough, impartial bibliography to support accessibility and utility as reference works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand field methods by observing them in practice
rubrics_metrics.description: “it never will be well understood without seeing the work going on on board ship; many men of science… have seen how quickly the sampler may be used… I should be glad to welcome many more visitors… not only to see the bottom-sampler working, but also to be able to discuss… the problems which have arisen in my mind while using this method.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complement written methodological descriptions with demonstrations or visits to operations in the field/lab to fully grasp practical constraints and capabilities.
